source.text: Ὃ ἦν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ὃ ἀκηκόαμεν, ὃ ἑωράκαμεν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν, ὃ ἐθεασάμεθα καὶ αἱ χεῖρες ἡμῶν ἐψηλάφησαν, περὶ τοῦ λόγου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ἑωράκαμεν καὶ μαρτυροῦμεν καὶ ἀπαγγέλλομεν ὑμῖν τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον ἥτις ἦν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα καὶ ἐφανερώθη ἡμῖν ὃ ἑωράκαμεν καὶ ἀκηκόαμεν ἀπαγγέλλομεν καὶ ὑμῖν, ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς κοινωνίαν ἔχητε μεθ’ ἡμῶν· καὶ ἡ κοινωνία δὲ ἡ ἡμετέρα μετὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: What was from beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with the eyes of us, what we beheld and the hands of us touched, concerning the word of the life—\v 2 and the life was revealed, and we have seen and we testify and we announce to you the life the eternal, which was toward the Father and was revealed to us—\v 3 what we have seen and we have heard we announce also to you, so that also you fellowship may have with us; and the fellowship and the ours [is] with the Father and with the Son of him Jesus Christ;

en.L: What was from [the] beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we beheld and our hands touched, concerning the word of life—\v 2 and the life was revealed, and we have seen [it] and testify and announce to you the eternal life, which was with the Father and was revealed to us—\v 3 what we have seen and heard we announce also to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us; and the fellowship that is ours [is] indeed with the Father and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: What was there from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our own eyes, what we looked at closely and touched with our hands—this is what we are speaking about: the word of life. \v 2 That life was revealed. We have seen it, and we testify to it, and we announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us. \v 3 We announce to you as well what we have seen and heard, so that you too may have fellowship with us. The fellowship we share is with the Father and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: We are writing to you about something that was there from the very beginning. We have heard it. We have seen it with our own eyes. We looked at it closely and touched it with our hands. We are telling you the message about life. \v 2 This life was shown to us openly. We have seen it, and we are witnesses who tell you about it. It is the eternal life that was with the Father and has now been shown to us. \v 3 We are telling you what we have seen and heard, so that you can share our life together with us. And our life together is with the Father and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Ce qui était depuis le commencement, ce que nous avons entendu, ce que nous avons vu de nos yeux, ce que nous avons contemplé et ce que nos mains ont palpé, au sujet de la parole de vie — \v 2 et la vie a été manifestée, et nous [l’]avons vue, et nous rendons témoignage et nous vous annonçons la vie éternelle, qui était auprès du Père et qui nous a été manifestée — \v 3 ce que nous avons vu et entendu, nous vous l’annonçons à vous aussi, afin que vous aussi, vous ayez communion avec nous ; et la communion qui est la nôtre [est] avec le Père et avec {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Ce qui existait depuis le commencement, ce que nous avons entendu, ce que nous avons vu de nos propres yeux, ce que nous avons regardé attentivement et touché de nos mains, voilà de quoi nous parlons : la parole de vie. \v 2 Cette vie a été manifestée. Nous l’avons vue, nous en rendons témoignage, et nous vous annonçons la vie éternelle qui était auprès du Père et qui nous a été manifestée. \v 3 Ce que nous avons vu et entendu, nous vous l’annonçons à vous aussi, afin que vous aussi soyez en communion avec nous. Et cette communion que nous partageons, c’est avec le Père et avec {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Nous vous écrivons au sujet de quelque chose qui existait déjà au tout début. Nous l’avons entendu. Nous l’avons vu de nos propres yeux. Nous l’avons regardé de près et nous l’avons touché de nos mains. Nous vous parlons du message qui donne la vie. \v 2 Cette vie nous a été montrée au grand jour. Nous l’avons vue, et nous sommes des témoins qui vous en parlent. C’est la vie éternelle, qui était auprès du Père et qui nous a maintenant été montrée. \v 3 Nous vous racontons ce que nous avons vu et entendu, pour que vous puissiez, vous aussi, partager la vie que nous vivons ensemble. Et cette vie, nous la partageons avec le Père et avec {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

es.L: Lo que era desde [el] principio, lo que hemos oído, lo que hemos visto con nuestros ojos, lo que contemplamos y tocaron nuestras manos, acerca de la palabra de vida—\v 2 y la vida fue manifestada, y [la] hemos visto y damos testimonio y {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos la vida eterna, que estaba con el Padre y nos fue manifestada—\v 3 lo que hemos visto y oído {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} anunciamos también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} comunión con nosotros; y la comunión nuestra [es] ciertamente con el Padre y con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Lo que existía desde el principio, lo que hemos oído, lo que hemos visto con nuestros propios ojos, lo que observamos de cerca y tocamos con nuestras manos: de esto hablamos, de la palabra de vida. \v 2 Esa vida se manifestó. La hemos visto, damos testimonio de ella y {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos la vida eterna, que estaba con el Padre y se nos manifestó. \v 3 {{plural_you:Les|Os}} anunciamos también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo que hemos visto y oído, para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} comunión con nosotros. Y la comunión que tenemos es con el Padre y con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} escribimos acerca de algo que existía desde el mismo principio. Lo hemos oído. Lo hemos visto con nuestros propios ojos. Lo miramos de cerca y lo tocamos con nuestras manos. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} contamos el mensaje acerca de la vida. \v 2 Esta vida se nos mostró abiertamente. La hemos visto, y somos testigos que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablamos de ella. Es la vida eterna que estaba con el Padre y que ahora se nos ha mostrado. \v 3 {{plural_you:Les|Os}} contamos lo que hemos visto y oído, para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:compartan|compartáis}} con nosotros nuestra vida en común. Y nuestra vida en común es con el Padre y con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kile kilichokuwapo tangu mwanzo, kile tulichokisikia, kile tulichokiona kwa macho yetu, kile tulichokitazama na mikono yetu ikakigusa, kuhusu neno la uzima—\v 2 na uzima ulidhihirishwa, nasi tumeuona, na tunashuhudia, na tunawatangazia ninyi uzima wa milele, ambao ulikuwa pamoja na Baba na ukadhihirishwa kwetu—\v 3 kile tulichokiona na kukisikia tunawatangazia ninyi pia, ili ninyi pia mpate kuwa na ushirika pamoja nasi; na ushirika wetu [ni] pamoja na Baba na pamoja na Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kile kilichokuwapo tangu mwanzo, tulichokisikia, tulichokiona kwa macho yetu wenyewe, tulichokitazama kwa makini na kukigusa kwa mikono yetu: hicho ndicho tunachozungumzia, yaani neno la uzima. \v 2 Uzima huo ulidhihirishwa. Tumeuona, tunaushuhudia, na tunawatangazia uzima wa milele uliokuwa pamoja na Baba na ukadhihirishwa kwetu. \v 3 Tunawatangazia ninyi pia yale tuliyoyaona na kuyasikia, ili nanyi mwe na ushirika pamoja nasi. Na ushirika tulio nao ni pamoja na Baba na pamoja na Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Tunawaandikia kuhusu kitu kilichokuwapo tangu mwanzo kabisa. Tumekisikia. Tumekiona kwa macho yetu wenyewe. Tulikitazama kwa makini na kukigusa kwa mikono yetu. Tunawaambia ujumbe kuhusu uzima. \v 2 Uzima huu ulionyeshwa kwetu waziwazi. Tumeuona, na sisi ni mashahidi tunaowaambia habari zake. Ni uzima wa milele uliokuwa pamoja na Baba, na sasa umeonyeshwa kwetu. \v 3 Tunawaambia yale tuliyoyaona na kuyasikia, ili nanyi mshirikiane nasi katika maisha haya. Na ushirika wetu ni pamoja na Baba na pamoja na Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: an echo of the opening of John's Gospel
decisions.reason: The opening gathers the words of John 1:1-4: "beginning" (ἀρχῆς), "word" (λόγου), "life" (ζωῆς), and a life that "was with the Father" (ἦν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα), as the Word "was with God" with the same preposition. "We have seen" and "we beheld" recall John 1:14, "we beheld his glory". Through John 1:1 the words also reach back to Genesis 1:1. Every level keeps the repeated words so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: from the beginning: before anything was made, as 1:2 says the life "was with the Father"
alternatives: from the beginning of the gospel, when the readers first heard it (as "from the beginning" means in 2:7, 24 and 3:11)
from the beginning of Jesus's ministry
decisions.reason: The letter uses the phrase in more than one way. Here it stands at the head of a sentence that echoes John 1:1 and goes on to say that the eternal life was with the Father before it was revealed (1:2), so it most likely reaches back before creation. But the same writer uses it for the beginning of the readers' faith, and the two may be meant together: the message they first heard is about the one who existed from the beginning.

decisions.choice: what, not who: the writer speaks of a thing, not yet of a person
alternatives: who: the relative words refer to Christ as a person
decisions.reason: Each Ὃ is neuter. The writer could have written "the one who", and does not. The neuter takes in everything about the life that was revealed: the person they saw and touched and the message they heard from him. Every level keeps speaking of a thing here, not yet of a person.

decisions.choice: the word of life: the message about the life, and the life is Christ himself
alternatives: the Word who is life: Christ himself, called "the Word" as in John 1:1, 14
decisions.reason: λόγου can mean a message or, as in John 1:1, the Word in person. Here the phrase is introduced by "concerning", and verse 2 goes on with "the life", not "the word", as the one revealed, so the word is most likely the message whose subject is that life. Elsewhere in the letter the word is the message God has spoken (1:10; 2:5, 7, 14). Since the life is Christ (1:2; 5:11-12, 20), both readings point to him; the difference is whether "word" is a title here.

decisions.choice: verse 2 interrupts the sentence, and verse 3 picks it up again
alternatives: one continuous sentence with "we announce to you" in verse 2 as its main verb
decisions.reason: The objects in verse 1 have no verb. Verse 2 breaks off to explain what "the life" is, and verse 3 starts again with "what we have seen and heard" (ὃ ἑωράκαμεν καὶ ἀκηκόαμεν) and finally gives the main verb, "we announce" (ἀπαγγέλλομεν). The broken shape shows the writer's urgency; Literal keeps it with dashes, and Balanced and Readable divide it into sentences.

decisions.choice: physical eyewitness: the life was heard, seen, looked at and touched
decisions.reason: The verbs rise from hearing to touching. ἐψηλάφησαν means to feel or handle with the hands; the risen Jesus uses the same verb in Luke 24:39 ("touch me and see"). Against any claim that the Son of God only seemed to be human (4:2-3), the writer says the life was something they handled. The perfect tenses ("we have heard", "we have seen") say what they still know; the aorists ("we beheld", "touched") point to particular moments.

decisions.choice: the life is Christ, who was with the Father and was revealed in his coming
alternatives: life as a gift or quality only, not a person
decisions.reason: ἐφανερώθη means "was made visible, was revealed"; the letter uses it of the Son's coming (3:5, 8) and of his return (2:28). The eternal life "was with the Father" before it was revealed, which only a person can be, and 5:20 calls Jesus Christ "the true God and eternal life". This life is also what believers are given (5:11-12).

decisions.choice: we: the eyewitnesses, among whom the writer counts himself; you: the readers
alternatives: we: the whole Christian community, including the readers
we: the writer alone, speaking in the plural
decisions.reason: "We" are set against "you" ("we announce to you", "so that you too may have fellowship with us"), so the readers are not included. The claim to have heard, seen and touched is a claim to have been there. Later in the letter "we" usually means all believers together (1:6-10); here it is the witnesses.

decisions.choice: fellowship: a shared life, partnership in something held in common
alternatives: friendly company or social time together
decisions.reason: κοινωνίαν means sharing in something together with others. The readers are to share with the witnesses, and what the witnesses share is a common life with the Father and the Son. It is more than good company: it is taking part in the same life. The phrase καὶ ἡ κοινωνία δὲ ἡ ἡμετέρα ("and indeed our fellowship") adds weight: this is what makes the fellowship worth having.

decisions.choice: the word of life (lowercase)
decisions.reason: Lowercase follows meaning decision m4: the word is the message about the life. A capital would make it a title of Christ, as in John 1:1. The footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: this is what we are speaking about (B); We are writing to you about ... We are telling you (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek holds its objects in suspense until verse 3 (meaning decision m5). An English sentence cannot wait that long, so Balanced supplies "this is what we are speaking about" and Readable starts with "We are writing to you about". Both say only what verse 3 says.

decisions.choice: the message about life
decisions.reason: "Word" for a message is not plain for young readers. Readable says "message", which follows meaning decision m4.

decisions.choice: share our life together
decisions.reason: "Fellowship" is church language. Readable says what it is (meaning decision m9): a life shared with others and with the Father and the Son. The same words are used in 1:6-7.

decisions.choice: testify; announce
decisions.reason: "Testify" is used for μαρτυρέω as in John 1:7 and 3:11. "Announce" is kept for ἀπαγγέλλω, so that the verb of 1:5 (ἀναγγέλλω), a near synonym, can be "declare".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son; Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun and title settings. "His" refers to the Father.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole book)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: 1 John is a letter: the writer speaks to his readers about what the witnesses heard, saw and touched, and French uses the passé composé for that ("nous avons entendu", "la vie a été manifestée"), as in Colossians and 2 John. The letter tells no story that would call for the passé simple.

decisions.choice: la parole de vie (L, B); le message qui donne la vie (R)
decisions.reason: John's Gospel uses "le Verbe" for the title of Christ (John 1:1). Here the word is first the message about the life (m4), so French uses the ordinary noun "parole", lowercase, as the English keeps "word" lowercase; "le Verbe de vie" would make it a title. Readable says "message", as the English does.

decisions.choice: communion, être en communion (L, B); partager la vie (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The word is a life held in common (m9). "Communion" is the established French word and keeps one word for 1:3, 1:6 and 1:7; Readable says what it is, as the English Readable's "share our life together" does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils; "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L), "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians and 2 John: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the span, subject "il" included, with the possessive agreeing with the noun; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital. "Jesus Christ" is written without the usual hyphen so that both options read naturally, and an article before the title stays outside the span ("le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}").

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: John writes to his readers in the plural. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in 1 John 5 and John's Gospel.

decisions.choice: la palabra de vida (lowercase)
decisions.reason: John's Gospel calls Christ "el Verbo" (John 1:1). Here the phrase is first the message about the life (meaning decision m4), so Spanish says "palabra" in lowercase, as the English says "word". The echo of the Gospel is left to the meaning note. "Luz", "vida", "mundo" and "permanecer" are the words of Spanish John throughout this letter.

decisions.choice: comunión (L, B); vida en común (R)
decisions.reason: In Philippians "comunión" was avoided for working partnership in the gospel. Here the word is a shared life with the Father and the Son and with one another (meaning decision m9), and "tener comunión" is the natural Spanish for that; Readable says "vida en común" and "compartir la vida", as the English says "share life".

decisions.choice: kile ... kilichokuwapo, tulichokisikia (class 7, a thing)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "what", not "who" (m3): the writer speaks of a thing before he names the person. The class 7 forms "kile", "kilichokuwapo", "tulichokiona" keep it a thing, as the English "what" does; the personal forms would name Christ too early.

decisions.choice: uzima; neno la uzima; uzima wa milele
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel and 1 John 5: "uzima" is life itself, the life of God (m7), while "maisha" is a lifetime or daily living. "Neno" is lowercase here, as the English "word of life" is.

decisions.choice: ushirika (L, B, and R in the second clause); mshirikiane nasi (R)
decisions.reason: Fellowship is a shared life held in common (m9). "Ushirika" is the church word for it and is used at every level; Readable first says it with the verb "kushirikiana" (share together), as the English Readable says "share our life together".

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb, and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("wake", "yake", "kwake", "naye"). Swahili has fewer spans than English in this letter.

source.text: καὶ ταῦτα γράφομεν ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡμῶν ᾖ πεπληρωμένη.

records.literal_gloss: And these things write we, so that the joy of us may be having been made full.

en.L: And these things we ourselves write, so that our joy may be made complete.
en.B: We put these things in writing so that our joy may be complete.
en.R: We are writing this so that our joy can be full.

fr.L: Et ces choses, nous-mêmes nous les écrivons, afin que notre joie soit rendue complète.
fr.B: Nous mettons ces choses par écrit pour que notre joie soit complète.
fr.R: Nous écrivons cela pour que notre joie soit pleine.

es.L: Y estas cosas escribimos nosotros, para que nuestro gozo esté completo.
es.B: Ponemos esto por escrito para que nuestra alegría sea completa.
es.R: Escribimos esto para que nuestra alegría sea plena.

sw.L: Na mambo haya tunayaandika sisi wenyewe, ili furaha yetu ipate kukamilika.
sw.B: Tunayaandika mambo haya ili furaha yetu iwe kamili.
sw.R: Tunaandika haya ili furaha yetu ijae.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "our joy"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts divide between "our" and "your", which sounded nearly alike when Greek was read aloud. "Our" is read by important early manuscripts, including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus; "your" is read by others, including Codex Alexandrinus, and by most later manuscripts, and stands in the King James Version. "Your" is the easier reading, since a writer would naturally hope for his readers' joy (compare John 16:24), so a copyist was more likely to change "our" to "your" than the reverse. The writer's joy is complete when the readers share the fellowship, so the two readings come close in meaning. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "we" as the subject, with no "to you"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, mostly later ones, read "we write to you" in place of the emphatic "we". The SBLGNT follows the early manuscripts that have "we". The letter is written to the readers either way. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: our joy is complete when the readers share the fellowship
alternatives: the writers' private joy, apart from the readers
decisions.reason: The emphatic ἡμεῖς ("we ourselves") picks up the witnesses of 1:1-3. Their joy is linked to the purpose just given in verse 3, that the readers may share their fellowship. The same words for joy made complete are in Jesus's promise in John 15:11 and 16:24, and in 2 John 12. The perfect participle πεπληρωμένη speaks of joy filled up and staying full.

decisions.choice: these things: the letter now being written
decisions.reason: The present tense "we write" points to the letter as a whole, which states its purposes in the same way later (2:1, 12-14, 26; 5:13).

decisions.choice: we ourselves
decisions.reason: The Greek adds the pronoun ἡμεῖς to a verb that already says "we", which gives it weight. Literal shows the emphasis; Balanced and Readable leave it to the word order.

decisions.choice: made complete (L); complete (B); full (R)
decisions.reason: "Complete" as in John 3:29. Readable uses the simpler "full".

decisions.choice: gozo (L); alegría (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians: Literal says "gozo", Balanced and Readable the everyday "alegría", both for the same word.

decisions.choice: sisi wenyewe
decisions.reason: The Greek writes the pronoun "we" though the verb already shows it, which makes it emphatic. Literal adds "wenyewe" (ourselves), as the English Literal says "we ourselves"; Balanced and Readable leave it in the verb.

source.text: Καὶ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ ἀγγελία ἣν ἀκηκόαμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναγγέλλομεν ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς φῶς ἐστιν καὶ σκοτία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν οὐδεμία.

records.literal_gloss: And is this the message which we have heard from him and we declare to you, that the God light is and darkness in him not is, none.

en.L: And this is the message which we have heard from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and declare to you, that God is light, and there is no darkness in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, none at all.
en.B: Now this is the message we heard from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and are declaring to you: God is light, and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there is no darkness, not the least.
en.R: Here is the message we heard from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and now we are telling it to you: God is light. There is no darkness in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at all.

fr.L: Et voici le message que nous avons entendu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et que nous vous déclarons : Dieu est lumière, et il n’y a pas de ténèbres en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, absolument aucune.
fr.B: Voici donc le message que nous avons entendu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et que nous vous déclarons : Dieu est lumière, et en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} il n’y a pas la moindre trace de ténèbres.
fr.R: Voici le message que nous avons entendu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et maintenant nous vous l’annonçons : Dieu est lumière. En {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, il n’y a pas du tout de ténèbres.

es.L: Y este es el mensaje que hemos oído de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos: que Dios es luz, y no hay en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} oscuridad alguna, ninguna.
es.B: Este es el mensaje que oímos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y que {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos: Dios es luz, y en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no hay oscuridad, ni la más mínima.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que oímos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y ahora {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} contamos: Dios es luz. En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no hay nada de oscuridad.

sw.L: Na huu ndio ujumbe tuliousikia kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} na tunaowatangazia ninyi, kwamba Mungu ni nuru, na ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hamna giza, hata kidogo.
sw.B: Basi ujumbe tuliousikia kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} na tunaowatangazia ni huu: Mungu ni nuru, na ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hamna giza hata kidogo.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe tuliousikia kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, nasi sasa tunawaambia ninyi: Mungu ni nuru. Ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hakuna giza lolote.

decisions.choice: from him: from Jesus, whom the witnesses heard
decisions.reason: The last person named is "his Son Jesus Christ" (1:3), and "what we have heard" (1:1, 3) is what the witnesses heard from Jesus. The message is about God, who is named next, so "him" is not God himself. Either way the message comes from God.

decisions.choice: God is light: wholly pure, true and good, and the one who makes himself known
decisions.reason: The sentence says what God is, as 4:8 says "God is love". In John's writings light is truth and goodness that shows things as they are (John 3:19-21), and the life that comes into the world (John 1:4-5; 8:12). Darkness is falsehood and evil. The next verses draw the moral meaning: to walk in darkness is to lie.

decisions.choice: no darkness at all: two negatives make the denial emphatic
decisions.reason: The Greek says "darkness in him is not, none", adding οὐδεμία after οὐκ. In Greek the second negative strengthens the first, and every level keeps the stress.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "message"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read a similar word meaning "promise". The SBLGNT reads "message" with the early manuscripts, and it matches the verb "we declare", which is built from the same root. The same phrase opens 3:11, "this is the message". Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: declare
decisions.reason: A different verb from "announce" in 1:2-3, close in meaning; Literal and Balanced keep the two verbs apart. Readable says "telling".

decisions.choice: from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting: both refer to God or Christ (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: il n’y a pas de ténèbres … absolument aucune (L); pas la moindre trace de ténèbres (B); pas du tout de ténèbres (R)
decisions.reason: French "ténèbres" is used only in the plural, so the Greek "no darkness, none" cannot be copied as "aucune ténèbre". Each level carries the doubled negative in its own way (m3), and "ténèbres" is kept at every level as the word set against "lumière" through 1:6 to 2:11.

decisions.choice: luz; oscuridad
decisions.reason: As in John 1:5 and 8:12, Spanish says "luz" and "oscuridad". "Tinieblas" is the older church word; "oscuridad" is the everyday one and is used for both Greek words for darkness in this letter.

decisions.choice: nuru; giza
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel: "nuru" is light as a figure for God's purity, truth and self-revelation (m2), while "mwanga" is everyday light. "Giza" is darkness. Both are kept through the letter.

source.text: ἐὰν εἴπωμεν ὅτι κοινωνίαν ἔχομεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ σκότει περιπατῶμεν, ψευδόμεθα καὶ οὐ ποιοῦμεν τὴν ἀλήθειαν·

records.literal_gloss: If we say that fellowship we have with him and in the darkness we walk, we lie and not we do the truth;

en.L: If we say that we have fellowship with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and walk in the darkness, we lie and do not do the truth.
en.B: If we claim to have fellowship with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while we go on walking in the darkness, we are lying and are not living by the truth.
en.R: Suppose we say that we share life with God, but we keep on living in the darkness. Then we are lying, and we are not living by the truth.

fr.L: Si nous disons que nous avons communion avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et que nous marchons dans les ténèbres, nous mentons et nous ne faisons pas la vérité.
fr.B: Si nous prétendons être en communion avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} alors que nous continuons à marcher dans les ténèbres, nous mentons et nous ne mettons pas la vérité en pratique.
fr.R: Supposons que nous disions partager la vie avec Dieu, mais que nous continuions à vivre dans les ténèbres. Alors nous mentons, et nous ne vivons pas selon la vérité.

es.L: Si decimos que tenemos comunión con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y andamos en la oscuridad, mentimos y no practicamos la verdad.
es.B: Si afirmamos tener comunión con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mientras seguimos andando en la oscuridad, mentimos y no vivimos según la verdad.
es.R: Supongamos que decimos que compartimos la vida con Dios, pero seguimos viviendo en la oscuridad. Entonces estamos mintiendo, y no vivimos según la verdad.

sw.L: Ikiwa tunasema kwamba tuna ushirika {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} na tunatembea gizani, tunasema uongo, wala hatuitendi kweli.
sw.B: Tukidai kwamba tuna ushirika {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} huku tukiendelea kutembea gizani, tunasema uongo, wala hatuishi kwa kufuata kweli.
sw.R: Huenda tukasema kwamba tunashirikiana na Mungu, lakini tunaendelea kuishi gizani. Hapo tunasema uongo, wala hatuishi kwa kufuata kweli.

decisions.choice: if we say: the first of three claims (1:6, 8, 10) the writer shows to be false
alternatives: general statements with no particular people in view
decisions.reason: Three sentences start "if we say", each followed by an answer (1:7, 9; 2:1). The claims may echo what those who had left the community were saying (2:19), but the writer puts them in the first person and so includes himself and his readers in the warning.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: To "walk" in a way is a Hebrew way of speaking about how a person lives (2:6, 11; John 8:12; 12:35). The present tense describes a settled way of life, not a single act.

decisions.choice: him: God, who is light (1:5)
decisions.reason: The sentence follows straight on from "God is light"; walking in darkness is set against fellowship with the God in whom there is no darkness.

decisions.choice: do the truth: live faithfully by what is true
decisions.reason: As in John 3:21, to "do the truth" is a Hebrew way of saying to act faithfully. The person who claims fellowship with God but lives in darkness lies with words and fails to live the truth in deeds.

decisions.choice: claim
decisions.reason: The three "if we say" sentences (1:6, 8, 10) introduce claims; Balanced says "claim" in all three. Literal and Readable keep "say".

decisions.choice: living by the truth
decisions.reason: "Do the truth" is not natural English. Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m4) and keep the key word "truth". Readable at John 3:21 says "lives by the truth" for the same idiom.

decisions.choice: share life with God; Suppose ... Then
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the one meant by "him" (meaning decision m3), uses the words for fellowship chosen at 1:3, and splits the condition into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting. Readable names God instead.

decisions.choice: nous ne faisons pas la vérité (L); nous ne mettons pas la vérité en pratique (B); nous ne vivons pas selon la vérité (R)
alternatives: nous ne pratiquons pas la vérité
decisions.reason: The same idiom as John 3:21 (m4), rendered there in French at the three levels in the same way, so that the two passages are heard together.

decisions.choice: andar (L, B); vivir (R); practicar la verdad (L); vivir según la verdad (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" means how one lives (meaning decision m2); Spanish "andar" has the same use, and Readable says "vivir". "Hacer la verdad" is not Spanish, so Literal says "practicar", and Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: tunatembea (L, B); kuishi (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" means how one lives (m2). Literal and Balanced keep the picture with the everyday verb "kutembea", as the English does; Readable says "kuishi" (live), as 2 John 4 does at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: hatuitendi kweli (L); hatuishi kwa kufuata kweli (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Do the truth" means to live by what is true (m4). Literal keeps "kutenda kweli", as John 3:21; Balanced and Readable say "live by following the truth", as the English does. "Kweli" is the key word for truth, as in John.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ ἐν τῷ φωτὶ περιπατῶμεν ὡς αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν τῷ φωτί, κοινωνίαν ἔχομεν μετ’ ἀλλήλων καὶ τὸ αἷμα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ καθαρίζει ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἁμαρτίας.

records.literal_gloss: If but in the light we walk as he is in the light, fellowship we have with one another and the blood of Jesus the Son of him cleanses us from all sin.

en.L: But if we walk in the light as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son cleanses us from all sin.
en.B: But if we walk in the light, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is in the light, we share fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, goes on cleansing us from every sin.
en.R: But suppose we live in the light, the way God is in the light. Then we share life with one another, and the blood of Jesus, God's Son, keeps making us clean from every sin.

fr.L: Mais si nous marchons dans la lumière comme {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} est dans la lumière, nous avons communion les uns avec les autres, et le sang de Jésus {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils nous purifie de tout péché.
fr.B: Mais si nous marchons dans la lumière, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est dans la lumière, nous sommes en communion les uns avec les autres, et le sang de Jésus, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, ne cesse de nous purifier de tout péché, quel qu’il soit.
fr.R: Mais supposons que nous vivions dans la lumière, comme Dieu est dans la lumière. Alors nous partageons la vie les uns avec les autres, et le sang de Jésus, le Fils de Dieu, continue à nous rendre purs de chacun de nos péchés.

es.L: Pero si andamos en la luz, como {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} está en la luz, tenemos comunión unos con otros, y la sangre de Jesús, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, nos limpia de todo pecado.
es.B: Pero si andamos en la luz, así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está en la luz, tenemos comunión unos con otros, y la sangre de Jesús, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, nos sigue limpiando de todo pecado.
es.R: Pero supongamos que vivimos en la luz, así como Dios está en la luz. Entonces compartimos la vida unos con otros, y la sangre de Jesús, el Hijo de Dios, nos sigue limpiando de todo pecado.

sw.L: Lakini tukitembea katika nuru kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alivyo katika nuru, tuna ushirika sisi kwa sisi, na damu ya Yesu, Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, inatusafisha kutoka katika dhambi yote.
sw.B: Lakini tukitembea katika nuru, kama vile {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo katika nuru, tuna ushirika sisi kwa sisi, na damu ya Yesu, Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, inaendelea kutusafisha kutoka kila dhambi.
sw.R: Lakini tukiishi katika nuru, kama Mungu alivyo katika nuru, tunashirikiana sisi kwa sisi. Nayo damu ya Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu, inaendelea kutusafisha kutoka kila dhambi.

decisions.choice: with one another: believers with each other
alternatives: we with God, and God with us
decisions.reason: ἀλλήλων means "one another", members of the same group. After 1:6 a reader might expect "fellowship with him"; instead the writer says that walking in the light shows itself in a shared life among believers, and the letter goes on to make love for one another the test (2:9-11; 3:11).

decisions.choice: the blood: Jesus's death as a sacrifice that takes away sin
alternatives: blood as a picture of his life, not his death
decisions.reason: In the Law, blood offered in sacrifice made atonement, and the Day of Atonement was given so that the people would be clean from all their sins before the Lord (Leviticus 16:30). The letter calls Jesus the atoning sacrifice for sins (2:2; 4:10). "Cleanses" is the language of that worship.

decisions.choice: cleanses: goes on cleansing, again and again
alternatives: a single cleansing in the past
decisions.reason: καθαρίζει is present tense. It describes what keeps happening for those who walk in the light, and fits the call to keep confessing sins (1:9).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Jesus his Son"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "Christ" after "Jesus", and the King James Version has it. Important early manuscripts have "Jesus" alone, and copyists tended to fill out the familiar full name. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: he, his: God, who is light, and whose Son Jesus is
decisions.reason: The sentence answers 1:6 and still has God in view (1:5).

decisions.choice: goes on cleansing (B); keeps making us clean (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the present tense (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the plain present.

decisions.choice: every sin
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article: each and every sin. Literal keeps "all sin".

decisions.choice: live; God; God's Son; suppose ... Then
decisions.reason: Readable explains "walk" (as at 1:6), names God (meaning decision m5) and splits the condition into two sentences.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting. Literal shows the emphatic αὐτός with "himself".

decisions.choice: kusafisha
decisions.reason: The verb is to make clean (m3). "Kusafisha" says that plainly; "kutakasa" also means to make holy, which is a different idea. The same verb is used in verse 9.

source.text: ἐὰν εἴπωμεν ὅτι ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἔχομεν, ἑαυτοὺς πλανῶμεν καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: If we say that sin not we have, ourselves we deceive and the truth not is in us.

en.L: If we say that we do not have sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
en.B: If we claim that we are free from sin, we are fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
en.R: If we say that there is no sin in our lives, we are only fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

fr.L: Si nous disons que nous n’avons pas de péché, nous nous égarons nous-mêmes, et la vérité n’est pas en nous.
fr.B: Si nous prétendons être sans péché, nous nous faisons des illusions, et la vérité n’est pas en nous.
fr.R: Si nous disons qu’il n’y a pas de péché dans notre vie, nous ne faisons que nous tromper nous-mêmes, et la vérité n’est pas en nous.

es.L: Si decimos que no tenemos pecado, nos engañamos a nosotros mismos, y la verdad no está en nosotros.
es.B: Si afirmamos que estamos libres de pecado, nos estamos engañando a nosotros mismos, y la verdad no está en nosotros.
es.R: Si decimos que no hay pecado en nuestra vida, solo nos estamos engañando, y la verdad no está en nosotros.

sw.L: Ikiwa tunasema kwamba hatuna dhambi, tunajipotosha wenyewe, na kweli haiko ndani yetu.
sw.B: Tukidai kwamba hatuna dhambi, tunajidanganya wenyewe, na kweli haimo ndani yetu.
sw.R: Tukisema kwamba hakuna dhambi maishani mwetu, tunajidanganya tu, na kweli haimo ndani yetu.

decisions.choice: have no sin: be free of sin and of guilt for it
alternatives: not be sinning at the moment
decisions.reason: "To have sin" is a phrase of John's for being guilty (John 9:41; 15:22, 24; 19:11). The claim is to be without sin altogether, so that there is nothing to confess. The letter elsewhere says believers do not go on sinning (3:6, 9), but never that they have no sin.

decisions.choice: deceive ourselves: lead ourselves astray
decisions.reason: πλανάω means to lead astray. The letter uses it of those who try to mislead the readers (2:26; 3:7). Here the people misled are the speakers themselves.

decisions.choice: the truth is not in us: God's truth has no place in our lives
decisions.reason: The truth is more than a correct statement; it is God's reality, which lives in those who know him (2:4; 2 John 2).

decisions.choice: claim
decisions.reason: As at 1:6.

decisions.choice: fooling ourselves
decisions.reason: Everyday English for the same idea. Literal keeps "deceive".

decisions.choice: tunajipotosha (L); tunajidanganya (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to lead astray (m2). Literal says "kujipotosha" (lead oneself off the way), the verb used for the deceivers in 2:26 and 2 John 7; Balanced and Readable say "kujidanganya" (fool oneself), as the English says "fooling ourselves".

source.text: ἐὰν ὁμολογῶμεν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, πιστός ἐστιν καὶ δίκαιος ἵνα ἀφῇ ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας καὶ καθαρίσῃ ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἀδικίας.

records.literal_gloss: If we confess the sins of us, faithful he is and righteous, so that he may forgive us the sins and may cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

en.L: If we confess our sins, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is faithful and righteous, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} forgives us [our] sins and cleanses us from all unrighteousness.
en.B: If we confess our sins, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is faithful and righteous: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will forgive our sins and cleanse us from every kind of wrongdoing.
en.R: If we admit our sins, God is faithful and righteous. He will forgive our sins and make us clean from every wrong thing we have done.

fr.L: Si nous confessons nos péchés, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est fidèle et juste, de sorte qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous pardonne les péchés et nous purifie de toute injustice.
fr.B: Si nous confessons nos péchés, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est fidèle et juste : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous pardonnera nos péchés et nous purifiera de toute forme de mal.
fr.R: Si nous reconnaissons nos péchés, Dieu est fidèle et juste. Il nous pardonnera nos péchés et nous rendra purs de tout le mal que nous avons fait.

es.L: Si confesamos nuestros pecados, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es fiel y justo, de modo que nos perdona los pecados y nos limpia de toda injusticia.
es.B: Si confesamos nuestros pecados, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es fiel y justo: nos perdonará los pecados y nos limpiará de toda maldad.
es.R: Si reconocemos nuestros pecados, Dios es fiel y justo. Él nos perdonará los pecados y nos limpiará de todo lo malo que hemos hecho.

sw.L: Ikiwa tunaziungama dhambi zetu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwaminifu na mwenye haki, kwa hiyo anatusamehe dhambi [zetu] na kutusafisha kutoka kila udhalimu.
sw.B: Tunapoungama dhambi zetu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwaminifu na mwenye haki: atatusamehe dhambi zetu na kutusafisha kutoka kila aina ya kosa.
sw.R: Tukikiri dhambi zetu, Mungu ni mwaminifu na mwenye haki. Atatusamehe dhambi zetu na kutusafisha kutoka kila jambo baya tulilofanya.

decisions.choice: confess: openly acknowledge our sins as sins
alternatives: make a general admission of being a sinner
decisions.reason: ὁμολογέω means to agree, to say the same thing, and so to acknowledge openly. It answers the denials of 1:8 and 1:10: instead of saying "we have no sin", we name our sins. The verse does not say before whom, though God is the one who forgives. The present tense describes a habit, not one occasion.

decisions.choice: faithful and righteous: God keeps his promises and acts rightly in forgiving
alternatives: faithful and just: fair as a judge, with no thought of promise
decisions.reason: God's faithfulness is his keeping of what he has promised (Deuteronomy 7:9; Hebrews 10:23); Deuteronomy 32:4 calls him faithful and righteous together. That he is righteous in forgiving may surprise; the letter's answer is the sacrifice of his Son (1:7; 2:1-2, where Jesus himself is "the righteous one"). Forgiveness comes from God's character, not in spite of it.

decisions.choice: so that: what his faithfulness and righteousness lead him to do
alternatives: purpose: he is faithful in order to forgive
decisions.reason: ἵνα here does not state a goal God aims at; it spells out what being faithful and righteous means for those who confess: he forgives and cleanses.

decisions.choice: he: God, who is light (1:5)
decisions.reason: The subject is unstated. God has been in view since 1:5, and 1:10 speaks of making him a liar, as 5:10 does of God. Jesus is named as the righteous advocate in 2:1, so a reference to him cannot be ruled out, but the forgiving is God's.

decisions.choice: unrighteousness: every wrong, everything that is not right
decisions.reason: ἀδικίας is the opposite of righteous, the word just used of God. The letter later says "all unrighteousness is sin" (5:17). Forgiveness removes the debt; cleansing removes the stain.

decisions.choice: righteous
decisions.reason: δίκαιος is rendered "righteous" at every level, so that it is heard as the same word that describes Jesus in 2:1 and 2:29 and is set against "unrighteousness" in this verse.

decisions.choice: every kind of wrongdoing (B); every wrong thing we have done (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "unrighteousness" to show the link with "righteous"; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the same thing.

decisions.choice: admit; God
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer "admit" and names God (meaning decision m4), and puts what he does in a second sentence.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: juste at every level; injustice (L), toute forme de mal (B), tout le mal que nous avons fait (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the New Testament, and as the English keeps "righteous" at every level: "juste" is the word used for Jesus in 2:1 and 2:29. Literal keeps "injustice" so that the link between the two words stays visible; Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: kuziungama dhambi (L, B); kukiri dhambi (R)
decisions.reason: To confess is to acknowledge one's sins openly as sins (m1). "Kuungama" is the word for confessing sins; Readable says "kukiri" (admit), as the English says "admit". "Kukiri" is kept for confessing the Son in 2:23 and 4:2-3.

decisions.choice: udhalimu (L); kila aina ya kosa (B)
decisions.reason: As in 1 John 5:17: "udhalimu" is the negative of right dealing and keeps the form of the Greek word at Literal; Balanced says "kosa" (any wrong act), since in everyday Swahili "udhalimu" often means oppression and would narrow the sense (m5).

source.text: ἐὰν εἴπωμεν ὅτι οὐχ ἡμαρτήκαμεν, ψεύστην ποιοῦμεν αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: If we say that not we have sinned, a liar we make him and the word of him not is in us.

en.L: If we say that we have not sinned, we make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a liar, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word is not in us.
en.B: If we claim that we have never sinned, we are calling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a liar, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word is not in us.
en.R: If we say that we have never sinned, we are saying that God is a liar. Then we do not have {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word in us.

fr.L: Si nous disons que nous n’avons pas péché, nous faisons de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un menteur, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole n’est pas en nous.
fr.B: Si nous prétendons n’avoir jamais péché, nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traitons de menteur, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole n’est pas en nous.
fr.R: Si nous disons que nous n’avons jamais péché, nous disons que Dieu est un menteur. Alors nous n’avons pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole en nous.

es.L: Si decimos que no hemos pecado, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hacemos mentiroso, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra no está en nosotros.
es.B: Si afirmamos que nunca hemos pecado, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} estamos llamando mentiroso, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra no está en nosotros.
es.R: Si decimos que nunca hemos pecado, estamos diciendo que Dios es mentiroso. Entonces no tenemos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra en nosotros.

sw.L: Ikiwa tunasema kwamba hatujatenda dhambi, tunamfanya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuwa mwongo, na neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} haliko ndani yetu.
sw.B: Tukidai kwamba hatujawahi kutenda dhambi, tunamwita mwongo, na neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} halimo ndani yetu.
sw.R: Tukisema kwamba hatujawahi kutenda dhambi, tunasema kwamba Mungu ni mwongo. Hapo hatuna neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ndani yetu.

decisions.choice: have not sinned: deny ever having sinned
alternatives: deny having sinned since becoming believers
decisions.reason: ἡμαρτήκαμεν is perfect: it looks back over the past from now. The claim in 1:8 was to have no sin now; this one denies any sin at all.

decisions.choice: make God a liar: contradict what God has said
decisions.reason: God has declared that all have sinned, and he sent his Son for sins (1:7; 4:10). To deny sin is to say God is wrong. 5:10 uses the same expression of refusing God's testimony about his Son.

decisions.choice: his word: God's message, the truth he has spoken
decisions.reason: λόγος here is what God has said, as "keeps his word" in 2:5 and "the word of God remains in you" in 2:14. It parallels "the truth is not in us" in 1:8.

decisions.choice: never sinned
decisions.reason: "Never" shows the scope of the perfect tense (meaning decision m1). Balanced says "claim" as at 1:6.

decisions.choice: we are saying that God is a liar
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what "make him a liar" amounts to.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: tunamfanya yeye kuwa mwongo
decisions.reason: As in 5:10: Literal writes the free pronoun "yeye" for the Greek pronoun, which makes plain that it is God who is made a liar (m2) and carries the deity_pronoun span. Balanced leaves the pronoun in the verb, as ordinary Swahili does.
